subproblem.title: Riesz representation (Simon 1.4.14) with a Borel measure and a Borel unit field on a σ-compact locally compact Hausdorff space
subproblem.statement: Let Y be a Hausdorff, locally compact, σ-compact topological space equipped with its Borel σ-algebra, N ∈ ℕ, H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), and L : C_c(Y, H) → ℝ an ℝ-linear map such that for every compact K ⊆ Y there is B ∈ ℝ with L(g) ≤ B for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H) with ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y and tsupport g ⊆ K. Then there are a (Borel) measure m on Y and a Borel measurable ν : Y → H such that m(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Y, ‖ν(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y, ‖ν(y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y, and L(g) = ∫_Y ⟨g(y), ν(y)⟩ dm(y) for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Y : Type) [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] [LocallyCompactSpace Y] [SigmaCompactSpace Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y] (N : ℕ) (L : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap Y (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set Y, IsCompact K → ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap Y (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → tsupport g ⊆ K → L g ≤ B) → ∃ (m : Measure Y) (ν : Y → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), (∀ K : Set Y, IsCompact K → m K < ∞) ∧ Measurable ν ∧ (∀ y, ‖ν y‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ᵐ y ∂m, ‖ν y‖ = 1) ∧ ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap Y (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), L g = ∫ y, inner ℝ (g y) (ν y) ∂m
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. Y is a Hausdorff, locally compact, σ-compact topological space whose σ-algebra is its Borel σ-algebra ([MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y], so measurable = Borel); H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), a finite-dimensional real inner product space, second countable, with its Borel σ-algebra; C_c(Y, H) = CompactlySupportedContinuousMap Y H. Outer-measure notions follow Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01 (Simon, Ch. 1): a set A is Carathéodory measurable for an outer measure μ₀ if μ₀(T) = μ₀(T ∩ A) + μ₀(T ∖ A) for all T. This is steps 4–7 of the parent proof of smr_riesz_borel_euclidean (Simon Ch. 1, 4.14 together with the completion/Borel-modification argument), stated for a general σ-compact locally compact Hausdorff space Y; the parent applies it to Y = ↥U.

1. (Riesz hypothesis.) For every compact K ⊆ Y the number B provided by the hypothesis is an upper bound of the set L''{g ∈ C_c(Y, H) : (∀ y, ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1) ∧ tsupport g ⊆ K}. Thus L satisfies Simon's local boundedness hypothesis of Ch. 1, 4.14 (IsLocallyBoundedCcFunctional L).

2. (Riesz representation, Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 4.14.) Since Y is locally compact Hausdorff and H is a finite-dimensional real inner product space, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_14 gives an outer measure μ₀ on Y with hμ₀ : IsRadonOuterMeasure μ₀ and a map ν₀ : Y → H such that (i) ν₀ is measurable from the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ₀ to the Borel σ-algebra of H; (ii) ‖ν₀(y)‖ = 1 for μ_C-a.e. y; (iii) L(g) = ∫ ⟨g(y), ν₀(y)⟩ dμ_C(y) for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H). Here μ_C := hμ₀.toCaratheodoryMeasure is μ₀ regarded as a measure on its Carathéodory σ-algebra. From IsRadonOuterMeasure we use: Borel regularity (every Borel set is Carathéodory measurable, and every A ⊆ Y has a Borel hull B ⊇ A with μ₀(B) = μ₀(A)), and finiteness on compact sets (μ₀(K) < ∞ for compact K). Moreover μ_C(A) = μ₀(A) for every A ⊆ Y (IsRadonOuterMeasure.toCaratheodoryMeasure_apply_all).

3. (The Borel measure m.) The σ-algebra of Y is the Borel σ-algebra, which is contained in the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ₀ (Borel regularity). Let m be the restriction of μ₀ to it, i.e. the measure m(A) = μ₀(A) for measurable A (m := μ₀.toMeasure hle with hle : Borel ≤ Carathéodory; this is hμ₀.borel_regular.toBorelMeasure). Claim: m(A) = μ₀(A) for every A ⊆ Y. Indeed m(A) ≥ μ₀(A), because the measure induced by an outer measure dominates it on all sets (le_toMeasure_apply); and if B ⊇ A is a Borel hull with μ₀(B) = μ₀(A), then m(A) ≤ m(B) = μ₀(B) = μ₀(A). Consequences:
(a) m(K) = μ₀(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Y.
(b) For every A ⊆ Y: m(A) = 0 ⟺ μ₀(A) = 0 ⟺ μ_C(A) = 0. As "Q holds a.e." means that the set where Q fails has measure 0, a property holds m-a.e. if and only if it holds μ_C-a.e.
(c) The trim of μ_C to the σ-algebra of Y equals m: for every Borel A, (μ_C.trim hle)(A) = μ_C(A) = μ₀(A) = m(A), and two measures agreeing on all measurable sets are equal.

4. (Carathéodory-measurable sets are m-null-measurable.) Write Y = ⋃_n K_n with K_n compact (σ-compactness). By local compactness each K_n has an open neighbourhood V_n with compact closure, and μ₀(V_n) ≤ μ₀(closure V_n) < ∞. Hence Y is covered by countably many open sets of finite μ₀-measure, i.e. μ₀ is open-σ-finite (isOpenSigmaFinite_of_finite_compacts hμ₀.finite_compacts). By IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.exists_borel_subset_mod_null, every Carathéodory-measurable A ⊆ Y contains a Borel set B with μ₀(A ∖ B) = 0. Then A = B ∪ (A ∖ B), where B is measurable and m(A ∖ B) = μ₀(A ∖ B) = 0 by step 3; a union of a measurable set and an m-null set is m-null-measurable, so A is m-null-measurable.

5. (A Borel version of ν₀.) For every Borel S ⊆ H, the set ν₀⁻¹(S) is Carathéodory measurable (step 2(i)), hence m-null-measurable (step 4); so ν₀ is m-null-measurable. Since H is second countable, its Borel σ-algebra is countably generated, and a null-measurable map into a countably generated measurable space is almost everywhere measurable (MeasureTheory.NullMeasurable.aemeasurable). Hence there is a Borel measurable ν₀′ : Y → H with ν₀(y) = ν₀′(y) for m-a.e. y.

6. (Normalized Borel field.) Define ν(y) := ν₀′(y) if ‖ν₀′(y)‖ = 1, and ν(y) := 0 otherwise. The set {y : ‖ν₀′(y)‖ = 1} is Borel (ν₀′ and the norm are measurable), so ν is Borel measurable. For every y, ‖ν(y)‖ equals ‖ν₀′(y)‖ = 1 or ‖0‖ = 0, so ‖ν(y)‖ ≤ 1. By step 2(ii) and step 3(b), ‖ν₀(y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y. For m-a.e. y both ν₀(y) = ν₀′(y) and ‖ν₀(y)‖ = 1 hold; for such y we get ‖ν₀′(y)‖ = 1, hence ν(y) = ν₀′(y) = ν₀(y) and ‖ν(y)‖ = 1. Thus ‖ν‖ = 1 m-a.e. and ν₀ = ν m-a.e.; by step 3(b) also ν₀ = ν μ_C-a.e. (the exceptional set {y : ν₀(y) ≠ ν(y)} is m-null, hence μ_C-null).

7. (Representation with Borel data.) Let g ∈ C_c(Y, H) and F(y) := ⟨g(y), ν(y)⟩. F is Borel measurable, since y ↦ (g(y), ν(y)) is measurable (g is continuous, hence Borel; ν is Borel) and the inner product H × H → ℝ is continuous, hence measurable for the product σ-algebra, which equals the Borel σ-algebra of H × H because H is second countable; F is real valued, hence strongly measurable for the σ-algebra of Y. Therefore
L(g) = ∫ ⟨g(y), ν₀(y)⟩ dμ_C(y)   (step 2(iii))
     = ∫ ⟨g(y), ν(y)⟩ dμ_C(y)    (the integrands agree μ_C-a.e. by step 6)
     = ∫ F d(μ_C.trim hle)        (integral_trim, F being strongly measurable for the smaller σ-algebra)
     = ∫ F dm                     (step 3(c)).

8. (Conclusion.) The pair (m, ν) satisfies: m(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Y (step 3(a)); ν is measurable (step 6); ‖ν(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y and ‖ν(y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y (step 6); and L(g) = ∫ ⟨g(y), ν(y)⟩ dm(y) for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H) (step 7). (No case distinction is needed for N = 0: then H = {0}, so ‖ν₀(y)‖ = 0 for every y and step 2(ii) forces μ_C(Y) = 0, hence m = 0 by step 3(b); all assertions still follow from steps 2–7.) ∎

proof_key_steps: The hypothesis gives IsLocallyBoundedCcFunctional L; apply simon_theorem_4_14 to get a Radon outer measure μ₀, its Carathéodory measure μ_C and a Carathéodory-measurable ν₀ with ‖ν₀‖ = 1 μ_C-a.e. and L g = ∫⟨g, ν₀⟩ dμ_C.
Let m be μ₀ restricted to the Borel σ-algebra of Y; Borel hulls give m(A) = μ₀(A) = μ_C(A) for all A ⊆ Y, so m is finite on compacts, m and μ_C have the same null sets, and μ_C.trim = m.
σ-compactness makes μ₀ open-σ-finite, so each Carathéodory-measurable set is a Borel set plus a μ₀-null set, hence m-null-measurable; thus ν₀ is m-null-measurable.
H is second countable, so ν₀ is m-a.e. equal to a Borel ν₀′ (NullMeasurable.aemeasurable); set ν := ν₀′ where ‖ν₀′‖ = 1 and 0 elsewhere: ν Borel, ‖ν‖ ≤ 1, ν = ν₀ and ‖ν‖ = 1 m-a.e. and μ_C-a.e.
L g = ∫⟨g, ν₀⟩ dμ_C = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ_C = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ d(μ_C.trim) = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dm by integral_congr_ae and integral_trim.
